assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation reframes small-molecule pharmacology: a molecule recruits an E3 ligase to a target, which is ubiquitylated and destroyed catalytically, reaching proteins previously considered undruggable. Original concept (PROTAC), clear chemical logic, and broad impact on medicinal chemistry and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies made the founding PROTAC concept and early demonstrations; Ciulli drove structure-guided, VHL-based and high-quality degrader design. Handa/Ito (thalidomide-cereblon mechanism, molecular glues) and others are also credited, so a three-person split leaves out a strong molecular-glue strand.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials and the mechanism is reproduced across many labs; no approved PROTAC drug yet, so recognition is slightly early but the science is solid and well confirmed.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be framed around PROTACs, molecular glues or both
Credit among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Ito and Gray is not cleanly separable
Absence of an approved degrader drug

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis, built on reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry and single-molecule detection, transformed biology and medicine and is arguably among the highest-impact analytical chemistry achievements of recent decades. The chemistry is original and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa/Illumina chemistry and single-molecule approach; Rothberg (pyrosequencing-based 454/Ion Torrent) and Mayer/Ju represent parallel or alternative technologies. Two laureates is a coherent core, but the field has several routes and the dispute over where the decisive contribution lies is genuine.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: technology used universally for over fifteen years, independently confirmed at enormous scale. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Competing technologies (454, Ion Torrent, nanopore) complicate the credit
Whether the committee views the achievement as chemistry rather than biology or technology
I rely on recalled history, not independent verification of priority claims

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites rose from sensitizer to solar absorbers exceeding 26% efficiency within about fifteen years, a striking case of materials chemistry with strong semiconductor-physics content. The impact on photovoltaics research is large, and the underlying defect tolerance and optoelectronic properties have been widely studied.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskite as a sensitizer (2009); Park achieved the first solid-state, stable device (2012); Snaith demonstrated the thin-film and meso-superstructured high-efficiency architecture. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are also strong, so any three-person selection leaves someone with a legitimate claim.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and reproducibility are well confirmed, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability remain open, so recognition may be somewhat premature compared with the science's scientific maturity.
uncertainties: Operational stability and scale-up are unresolved
Many strong contributors beyond three
Priority between Miyasaka, Park, Snaith and Grätzel

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA or RNA molecules electrically through a nanopore is a conceptually elegant union of molecular engineering and nanofluidics, and it has produced a widely used long-read sequencing technology. It is close to my own field of nanoscale transport and I judge it as a true instrument-level invention with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Akeson conceived the idea of nanopore strand sequencing; Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide translocation; Bayley engineered protein pores and Akeson showed enzymatic control that made base reading practical. Credit is spread over five names, so the prize configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices in routine use and independently validated, though accuracy has only recently reached parity for some applications; maturity is good and improving.
uncertainties: Allocation among Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz, Akeson and Bayley is contested
Potential perception as an overlap with the sequencing field if B014 were awarded
My field proximity may bias me toward nanopore work

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami demonstrated programmable folding of long DNA into arbitrary two- and three-dimensional shapes with nanometer precision, opening molecular nanotechnology, nanoscale templating and nanomechanical devices. It is original, clear and has had broad influence across chemistry, physics and bioengineering.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced scaffolded DNA origami in 2006; Seeman's earlier structural DNA nanotechnology (not on this list) is foundational, which complicates fair credit. Among the credited names, Yan and others extended origami to 3D and complex structures, while Winfree, Yin and Shih made major contributions in algorithmic assembly and 3D designs.
assessment.maturity: The method is reproduced worldwide, but applications beyond demonstrations are still emerging, so impact is mostly conceptual and methodological so far.
uncertainties: The founder of structural DNA nanotechnology, Seeman, is deceased and not on the list, which weakens the attribution picture
Real-world applications remain limited
Credit among Rothemund, Yan, Yin, Shih and Winfree is not settled

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another at a target locus without double-strand breaks, a conceptually clean piece of molecular design with direct therapeutic consequences, including clinical trials. Strongly chemical in nature.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the design and conception; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead first-author contributors to cytosine and adenine base editors. A fair configuration is Liu alone or Liu with the two postdoctoral authors; Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID) developed a parallel approach.
assessment.maturity: Early clinical results are very promising but long-term safety data are limited, and since CRISPR has already been recognized, the committee might see this as a follow-on; timing is plausible but not yet settled.
uncertainties: Long-term clinical safety and efficacy are not yet established
Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with B068
Whether trainee contributors should be named

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C mutant with a cysteine-reactive inhibitor, together with earlier analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics, broke the long-standing view of KRAS as undruggable and led to approved drugs. A clean chemistry-driven discovery with direct patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the single credited name, who led the decisive KRAS G12C tethering work and the kinase chemical genetics; the clinical drugs were later developed by Amgen and Mirati, which complicates any wider attribution of the drug story.
assessment.maturity: Approved sotorasib and adagrasib provide strong independent validation, though resistance and durability limit the response; recognition would be timely but not urgent.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry or pharmacology
Industrial development credit lies outside the listed name
Durability of clinical responses

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near-quantum accuracy at classical cost, enabling large-scale simulation of materials and reactions. For someone from a physics background, the unifying methodology and its reach across materials, molecules and nanostructures are compelling.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello introduced neural-network potentials with symmetry functions (2007); Bartók and Csányi introduced Gaussian approximation potentials; many others, including von Lilienfeld and E, contributed. The prize configuration is challenging because the field is large and rapidly evolving.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly developing and now widely used, but model transferability and reliability remain active research questions; lasting significance is likely and the timing is perhaps a few years early.
uncertainties: Rapid evolution of the field makes the foundational claims unstable
Many contributors, including Weinan E and von Lilienfeld
Parrinello's own separate candidacies (B004, B053) may complicate the assignment
